αὐτίκ: αὐτίκα (elided αὐτίκ’) — at once, immediately, forthwith; adv.
αὐτοῖο: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ): ’himself’
αὖθ: αὖθι (elided αὖθ’) — here, on the spot, right here; adv. (distinct from αὖτε/αὖ ’again, in turn’) · also = αὖτε ’again, in turn’, marking the next item of a series (χωρὶς δ’ αὖθ’ ἕρσαι ’and again separately, the youngest’) · also with αἰεί, ’hereafter, henceforth’ (αἰεὶ αὖθ’ ἡμῖν μεταδαίσεται ’always hereafter he shall feast among us’)
βάλλον: βάλλω — throw, cast; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= Attic ἔβαλλον): ’were casting, threw’
βάτην: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 dual, unaugmented (= ἐβήτην)
βίην: βίη — strength, might, force; fem. acc. sg.
βαρὺ: βαρύς — heavy, deep; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’heavily’
βασιλῆα: βασιλεύς — king; acc. sg., epic βασιλῆα (= Attic βασιλέα)
βασιλῆος: βασιλεύς — king; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έως)
γένηται: γίγνομαι — come to be, happen; aor. subj. 3 sg., in a temporal clause with ἄν/κε: ’shall come’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a direct question of doubt/deliberation, no ἄν/κε: τί … γένηται; ’what is to happen?’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg., prospective in a negative statement with a relative clause: οὐδὲ γένηται ’nor ever shall there be’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a general relative clause without ἄν/κε: ’whatever shall come to pass’ (ὅσσα γένηται) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a fear clause after μή: ’lest it become’ (μή … ἕλωρ … γένηται ’lest it become prey’) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in an indirect clause after ὅπως: ’(consider) how it may turn out’ (ὅπως ὄχ’ ἄριστα γένηται) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. with κε, in a conditional or relative clause: ’shall prove, become’ (ὁππότερος … κε νικήσῃ κρείσσων τε γένηται; αἴ κέν … γένηται)
γέροντι: γέρων — old man; masc. dat. sg.
γήθησεν: γηθέω — rejoice; aor. 3 sg., ν-movable (= γήθησε): ’rejoiced’
γούνων: γόνυ — knee; neut. gen. pl., epic γούνων (= Attic γονάτων)
δάκρυ: δάκρυ — tear; neut. acc. sg., used collectively: ’tears’ · also elided δάκρυ’ = δάκρυα, neut. acc. pl. · also literal sg. with an attributive adjective, not collective: θαλερὸν δάκρυ ’a swelling tear’ · also literal sg., no adjective: ’a tear’ (ἀπομόρξατο δάκρυ ’wiped away a tear’)
δία: Ζεύς — Zeus; masc. acc. sg. Δία
δακρύσας: δακρύω — weep, shed tears; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having wept’
δεσμῶν: δεσμός — bond, fetter; masc. gen. pl. (ἐκ δεσμῶν ’out of the bonds’)
δύνασαί: δύναμαι — be able, can; pres. 2 sg. mid., accented before an enclitic
δὸς: δίδωμι — give, grant; aor. imper. 2 sg.
δῶκε: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔδωκε)
εἰδὼς: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’knowing’
εἴδομεν: οἶδα — know; perf. subj. 1 pl., short-vowel (= Attic εἰδῶμεν), hortatory: ’let us know, let us find out’ · also ὁράω — see; aor. 1 pl. εἴδομεν, augmented (the same form in Attic; εἶδον): indicative ’we saw’
εὐξαμένου: εὔχομαι — pray, vow; aor. part. mid. masc. gen. sg.: ’praying’
εὗρον: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ηὗρον) · also aor. 1 sg.: ’I found’ (εὗρον ἔπειτ’ … ἑταίρους)
θεοί: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θεράποντε: θεράπων — attendant, servant; masc. nom. dual
θῖν: θίς — shore, beach; masc. acc. sg., elided (θῖν’ = θῖνα)
κέλευθα: κέλευθος — path, way, course; neut. nom./acc. pl. κέλευθα, epic by-form beside fem. sg. κέλευθος
κίεν: κίω — go, go one’s way; impf. 3 sg., epic unaugmented (= ἔκιεν): ’went’
καθέζετο: καθέζομαι — sit down, seat oneself; impf. 3 sg.: ’sat down’
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ἦμαρ: ’evil’ (κακὸν ἦμαρ ’the evil day’) · also masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’base, cowardly’ (κακὸν καὶ ἀνήνορα ’base and unmanned’) · also neut. acc. sg. attributive with πῆμα: ’evil’ (πῆμα κακὸν ’evil harm’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: κακὸν … βάζειν ’(it is) bad to speak’ · also neut. acc. sg. governed by ἐς: ’into evil’ (ἐς κακὸν … βάλῃσθα) · also neut. acc. sg. subject of an infinitive: ’an evil’ (κακὸν ἔμμεναι ’that an evil is’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of εἴη: ’evil’ (μή τι κακὸν … εἴη ’and may no evil be’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ῥάκος: ’vile’ (ῥάκος ἄλλο κακὸν ’another, a vile rag’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a finite verb: ’an evil’ (ἐπεὶ κακὸν ἔμπεσεν οἴκῳ ’since an evil fell upon the house’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with γενοίμην: ’a bane, an evil (to them)’ · also masc. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’a base man’ (κακὸς κακὸν ἡγηλάζει) · also masc. acc. sg., attributive with θάνατον: ’evil’ (θάνατον … κακόν ’evil death’) · also masc. acc. sg., in apposition to τινα: ’bad (man)’ (οὐ κακὸν οὐδὲ … ἐσθλόν ’neither bad nor good’) · also neut. nom./acc. sg., attributive with τέλος: ’evil’ (κακὸν τέλος ’evil end’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with πόλεμον: ’evil’ (πόλεμόν τε κακόν ’evil war’)
καλέουσι: καλέω — call, name; pres. 3 pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic καλοῦσι)
καρπαλίμως: καρπάλιμος — swift, nimble; adv. καρπαλίμως: ’swiftly, nimbly’
κατέρεξεν: καταρρέζω — stroke, caress (with the hand); aor. 3 sg.
κελαινεφέϊ: κελαινεφής — dark-clouded (epithet of Zeus); adj., masc. dat. sg.
κελόμην: κέλομαι — urge, bid, command; impf. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἐκελόμην): ’I urged’
κεῦθε: κεύθω — hide, conceal; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’hide!’
κλαίεις: κλαίω — weep, lament; pres. 2 sg.: ’you weep’
κλισίης: κλισίη — hut, shelter; fem. gen. sg., Ionic -ίη (= Attic κλισία)
κλισίῃ: κλισίη — hut, shelter; fem. dat. sg., Ionic η
κνίση: κνίση — savour of burning fat; fem. nom. sg.
κτεινομένους: κτείνω — kill, slay; pres. part. pass. masc. acc. pl.: ’being killed’
λάβεν: λαμβάνω — take; aor. 3 sg. act., unaugmented, with movable ν (= ἔλαβεν)
λαοὶ: λαός — people, host, men of the community; masc. nom. pl.
μάκαρες: μάκαρ — blessed, happy (esp. of the gods); masc. nom. pl. · also voc. pl. in address: μάκαρες θεοί ’blessed gods!’
μάρτυροι: μάρτυς — witness; nom. pl., epic μάρτυροι (= Attic μάρτυρες)
μακάρων: μάκαρ — blessed, happy; masc. gen. pl., epithet of the gods
μακρὸν: μακρός — long, far; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’far, loudly’ · also masc. acc. sg. agreeing with a noun: ’tall’ (κίονα μακρὸν ’a tall pillar’) · also neut. nom. sg., agreeing with ἐέλδωρ: ’long’ (μακρὸν ἐέλδωρ ’long wish’)
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μυρμιδόνων: Μυρμιδόνες — the Myrmidons, Achilles’ people; masc. gen. pl.
νέον: νέος — new, young; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’newly, for the first time’ · also masc. acc. sg., ’young’ (νέον ἄνδρα ’a young man’) · also neut. nom./acc. sg., ’new’ (οὔ τι νέον ’not a new one’, of a debt) · also adv., ’just now, a moment ago’ (νέον ἠὲ πάροιθεν ’just now than before’; νέον ἦσθα γέρων ’just now you were an old man’)
νοῆσαι: νοέω — perceive, notice, take note of; aor. inf.: ’to glimpse, to notice’ · also ’think out, think of’ (πεπνυμένα πάντα νοῆσαι ’to think of all prudent things’)
νυ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
νόσφι: νόσφι — apart from, except (+ gen.); adv./prep.
οἴη: οἶος — alone, only; fem. nom. sg.
πάντ: πᾶς — all, every; neut. acc. pl. (elided πάντ’): ’everything’ · also masc. acc. sg., elided, agreeing with μῆνα: ’the whole (month)’
πάντῃ: πάντῃ — everywhere, in every direction; adv.
πάροιθ: πάροιθε(ν) — before, in front of; prep. + gen., elided (πάροιθ’ = πάροιθεν): ’before (her)’
πάτροκλος: Πάτροκλος — Patroclus, companion of Achilles, killed by Hector; masc. nom. sg.
πέμπουσιν: πέμπω — send, convey, escort; pres. 3 pl.
πένοντο: πένομαι — labor at, be busy with, toil; impf. 3 pl.
πέρ: περ — even, indeed; intensive/concessive particle, accented πέρ before the enclitic τε/τις that follows it; with εἰ: ’even if’
παιδὸς: παῖς — child, daughter; fem. gen. sg. (φίλης ... παιδός ’a dear daughter’) · also masc. gen. sg., ’son’ (παιδὸς ἐμοῖο ’my son’; τοῦ παιδὸς ἀγαυοῦ ’the noble son’) · also masc. gen. sg., ’boy, child’, with ἐόντος, gen. of the person described (παιδὸς ἐόντος ’when I was a boy’)
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, title of Athena of unknown origin (perhaps πάλλω ’brandish’); nom. sg.
παρά: παρά — beside, from beside; preverb standing apart from its verb in tmesis (παρά … ἤπαφε = παρήπαφε ’led astray’); accented before an enclitic · also prep. + dat., ’beside, among’ (παρά τε μνηστῆρσιν ’and among the suitors’)
πλεόνεσσι: πολύς — much, many; comparative πλέων/πλείων, masc. dat. pl. πλεόνεσσι, epic -εσσι (= Attic πλείοσι)
πολιῆς: πολιός — grey; fem. gen. sg., agreeing with ἁλός · also agreeing with θαλάσσης: ’the grey sea’ · also fem. gen. sg., agreeing with κεφαλῆς: ’grey (head)’
πολλάκι: πολλάκι(ς) — many times, often; adv., epic (= Attic πολλάκις)
ποσειδάων: Ποσειδῶν — Poseidon, god of the sea, enemy of Odysseus after the blinding of his son Polyphemus; nom. sg., epic uncontracted · also elided acc. sg., Ποσειδάων’ = Ποσειδάωνα: ’Poseidon’ as object
προΐει: προΐημι — send forth, send along; impf. 3 sg.: ’sent along’ · also pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’let fly!’ (προΐει δολιχόσκιον ἔγχος ’let fly your long-shadowed spear’)
προσεφώνεον: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεφώνουν)
πρός: πρός — in the name of, by; prep. + gen., in an entreaty; accented before τε
πρόσσω: πρόσω — forward, onward; adv., epic double σ (= Attic πρόσω)
πόντον: πόντος — sea, open sea; acc. sg.
πότνια: πότνια — lady, mistress (title of respect for a goddess); fem. nom. sg. · also of a mortal woman, a respectful title: ’revered, honoured’ (πότνια μήτηρ ’the honoured mother’)
στήτην: ἵστημι — set up; intrans. aor. stand; aor. 3 dual, root aorist (= Attic ἐστήτην): ’the two stood still’
στενάχων: στενάχω — groan, moan; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
σφίσιν: σφεῖς — they; epic dat. pl. pron. (= Attic αὐτοῖς), reflexive of the subject: ’for themselves’ · also dat. pl. after μετά, not reflexive: ’among them’ (μετὰ σφίσιν) · also dat. pl. indirect object, not reflexive: ’to them’
σφωϊν: σύ (dual σφῶϊ) — you two; dat. dual σφῶϊν (same form as gen.), epic (= Attic σφῷν): ‘to you two’
σφῶϊ: σύ — you; 2nd pers. dual nom. σφῶϊ, epic (= Attic σφώ): ’you two’
σόοι: σόος — safe, unharmed (epic = Attic σῶς); masc. nom. pl.
τέ: τε — and; enclitic connective, also marks a standing fact (epic τε) · also in the idiom ὅ τε (= ὅτι) ’in that, because’, giving a reason: ὅ τέ με … ἀποβῆναι ἀνώγει ’in that he bids me step off’ · also in ἦ τέ, a strengthened affirmation: ’truly’ (ἦ τέ μ’ ἔφαντο ’who truly said’) · also epic τε after ἵνα ’where’, with no connective force (ἵνα τε κρίνονται ’where they are decided’)
τέκνον: τέκνον — child; neut. voc. sg. (= nom./acc. in form)
τεληέσσας: τεληείς — complete, fulfilling, perfect (of sacrifice, from τέλος); adj., fem. acc. pl.
τοῖο: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun/demonstrative); masc./neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic τοῦ): ’of it, of that’
τοῖς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: masc./neut. dat. pl. ’in which, with which’ (τετυγμένα, τοῖς ἐνάμελγεν ’well-made, in which he milked’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. dat. pl.: ’the’ (ἰχθύσι τοῖς ὀλίγοισι ’for the little fishes’) · also demonstrative dat. pl. of things just named, ‘with these’ (τοῖς ἔξειμι ‘with these I shall go out’)
τρώεσσιν: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. dat. pl., ν-movable
τυτθὸν: τυτθός — small, little; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’when small’
τόν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg.: ’him’; also relative: ’whom’ · also demonstrative with a noun, ’that’, antecedent of a relative: ἄνδρα τόν, ὅς κε … ’that man who …’ · also masc. acc. sg. ’it’, of a thing (τόν ῥ’ ἐπὶ πήχει ἑλών ’taking it on the bow-grip’, of the arrow)
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. dual: ’the two of them’  ·  also acc. dual, object of a verb of address: τὼ … προσέφη ’spoke to the two of them’ · also relative, nom. dual, ’who (the two)’: τοκῆε δύω, τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον · also nom. dual with a noun, article-like: ’the two’ (τὼ … θεράποντε)
φίλος: φίλος — dear, dear one; masc. nom. sg. used as voc.: ’friend’ · also plain attributive adjective, not vocative: ’dear’ (φίλος υἱός ’dear son’) · also predicate adjective: ’dear’ (φίλος ἦεν Ἰήσων ’Jason was dear (to her)’)
φίλῃ: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. dat. sg.
φώνησέν: φωνέω — utter, speak aloud, call out; aor. 3 sg., accented φώνησέν before the enclitic τε
χέων: χέω — pour, shed; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
χαλκοχιτώνων: χαλκοχίτων — bronze-shirted, with tunic of bronze (χαλκός + χιτών); gen. pl.
χρειὼ: χρειώ — need, want, business; fem. nom. sg., epic by-form of χρεία; in τίνα χρειὼ … ἵκει ’whom has need come upon?’
χόλος: χόλος — anger, wrath; masc. nom. sg.
ἀέκοντε: ἄκων (ἀέκων) — unwilling; masc. nom. dual: ’the two unwilling’ (οὐκ ἀέκοντε ’not unwilling’)
ἀγέμεν: ἄγω — lead, drive; pres. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἄγειν)
ἀγορεύω: ἀγορεύω — speak, speak in assembly; pres. 1 sg.
ἀγόρευε: ἀγορεύω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἠγόρευε)
ἀμείνων: ἀγαθός — good; comparative ἀμείνων, masc. nom. sg.: ’better’
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’) · also + gen., ’about, concerning’ (ἀμφ’ Ἄρεος φιλότητος ’about the love of Ares’) · also with ὀστεόφιν, ’around’ (ἀμφ’ ὀστεόφιν θὶς ’a heap around the bones’)
ἀνέδυ: ἀναδύομαι — come up, emerge; aor. 3 sg., root aorist
ἀναβάντες: ἀναβαίνω — go up, go aboard, embark; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having embarked’
ἀναστὰς: ἀνίστημι — stand up, rise; intrans. aor. part. masc. nom. sg., root aorist: ’standing up’
ἀπείρονα: ἀπείρων — boundless, endless; fem. acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg. (the same form serves both genders for this adjective): ἀπείρονα πόντον ’boundless sea’
ἀπούρας: ἀπαυράω — take away, deprive; aor. part. masc. nom. sg., epic (ἀπούρας = ἀφελόμενος): ’having taken away’
ἀργείοισι: Ἀργεῖος — Argive, Greek; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀτρυγέτοιο: ἀτρύγετος — unharvested, restless (of the sea; exact sense uncertain); gen. sg., epic (-οιο = Attic -ου)
ἀχαιοὺς: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, i.e. the Greeks; acc. pl.
ἁλὸς: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. gen. sg. · also masc. gen. sg., with the masc. adjective πολιοῖο: ’of the grey sea’ (ἁλὸς πολιοῖο)
ἄγοντες: ἄγω — lead, bring; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’bringing, leading’
ἄκουσα: ἀκούω — hear; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἤκουσα)
ἄλλοις: ἄλλος — other, another; masc./neut. dat. pl.
ἄμμι: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; epic dat. pl. ἄμμι (= Attic ἡμῖν)
ἄνδρες: ἀνήρ — man; nom. pl. · also masc. voc. pl., in address: ’men!’ (ἄνδρες, ἐπεὶ κνίση μὲν ἀνήνοθεν)
ἄνωγεν: ἄνωγα (defective, perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; 3 sg., ν-movable, used with past narrative force (+ inf.): ’commands, bade’
ἄτην: ἄτη — ruinous blindness, delusion (sent by a god), ruin; fem. acc. sg.
ἆσσον: ἆσσον — nearer, closer; adv., comparative of ἄγχι
ἐθέλῃσιν: ἐθέλω — wish, want; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic ending -ῃσι
ἐλθοῦσ: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. part. fem. nom. sg., elided (ἐλθοῦσ’ = ἐλθοῦσα)
ἐλθοῦσα: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. part. fem. nom. sg.: ’having come, coming on’
ἐνθάδε: ἐνθάδε — here, to this place; adv., with -δε suffix of direction (’in this place’)
ἐπέπλεον: ἐπιπλέω — sail upon, sail over; impf. 3 pl.: ’were sailing over’
ἐπί: ἐπί — on, upon, towards; here as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἐπί ... ἤλυθεν = ἐπῆλθεν ’came on, came upon’); accented ἐπί before the following enclitic τε · also prep. + dat.: ’at, by’ (ἐπί τε κρήνῃ Ἀρεθούσῃ ’and at the spring Arethusa’)
ἐπασσύτεροι: ἐπασσύτερος — close one upon another, in quick succession; masc. nom. pl.
ἐρέοντο: ἐρέομαι — ask, inquire (often with ἐκ in tmesis, = ἐξερέοντο); impf. 3 pl. mid.: ’they asked’
ἑκατηβόλου: ἑκατηβόλος — far-shooting (epithet of Apollo; traditional sense); masc. gen. sg.
ἑκατόμβας: ἑκατόμβη — hecatomb, a great sacrifice (orig. of a hundred oxen); fem. acc. pl.
ἑλὼν: αἱρέω — take, seize, grasp; aor. act. part. masc. nom. sg. (ἑλών): ’having seized’
ἑτάρων: ἑταῖρος (epic ἕταρος) — companion, comrade; masc. gen. pl. (= Attic ἑταίρων)
ἑῆος: ἐΰς (ἠΰς) — good, noble; masc. gen. sg., epic ἑῆος/ἐῆος (= Attic ἀγαθοῦ)
ἔβαν: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔβησαν)
ἔδησαν: δέω — bind, make fast; aor. 3 pl.
ἔργῳ: ἔργον — deed, work, task; neut. dat. sg.
ἔστων: εἰμί — be; pres. imper. 3 pl.: ’let them be’
ἔτ: ἔτι — still, yet; adv., elided (ἔτ’ = ἔτι)
ἔφησθα: φημί — say, speak; impf. 2 sg., with the old ending -σθα (Attic ἔφησθα or ἔφης): ’you said’
ἕλον: αἱρέω — take, take down; aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic εἷλον) · also in the idiom ὀδὰξ ἕλον οὖδας ’bit the ground’, of falling dead
ἠρήσατο: ἀράομαι — pray, pray to; aor. 3 sg. mid. (augment ἀ- → ἠ-)
ἡμένη: ἧμαι — sit, be seated; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.
ἤ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj., accented before an enclitic (ἤ κεν); ἤ … ἦε ’whether … or’ · also ’than’ after a comparative: μεῖζον … ἤ ’greater than’ · also ’than’, ’rather than’, after a verb of preferring (βούλομ’ … ἤ τινα ’I prefer … to any’) · also the first of two alternatives, accented before an enclitic: ’either … or’ (ἤ ῥά νύ που … ἢ ὅ γ’ ’either … or’)
ἤγομεν: ἄγω — lead, bring; impf. 1 pl.: ’we led’
ἤθελον: ἐθέλω — be willing, wish; impf. 3 pl., augmented: ’they wished’
ἥμενον: ἧμαι — sit; pres. part. mid. masc. acc. sg., epic ἥμενος: ’sitting’
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἰδυίῃ: οἶδα — know; perf. part. fem. dat. sg., epic (= Attic εἰδυίᾳ): ’skilled, knowing’ + acc.
ἱκέσθην: ἱκνέομαι — come to, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 dual
ἴτην: εἶμι — go; impf. 3 dual (= Attic ᾔτην): ’the two went’
ἵκετο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 sg.; where the metre makes the ι long, that is the augment, which the spelling cannot show; with short ι, unaugmented
ὀλύμπιος: Ὀλύμπιος — Olympian, of Olympus; adj., masc. nom. sg. (epithet of Zeus)
ὀνόμαζε: ἐξονομάζω — call by name, address directly; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, tmesis (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζε = ἐξωνόμαζε) · also ὀνομάζω (simple, no preverb) — name, call by name, tell the name of; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’name (him)!’ (τρίτον ἄνδρ’ ὀνόμαζε)
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv. · also ’back, home again’, of return (οἴκαδ’ ὀπίσσω ’back home’)
ὁππότε: ὁππότε (Attic ὁπότε) — whenever, when; conj., + subj. and κε in a general temporal clause · also introducing an indirect question, + pres. indic.: ’when’ (ὁππότε Τηλέμαχος νεῖτ(αι) ’when Telemachus is to return’) · also + subj. without κε, in a general clause: ’whenever’ (ὁππότε τις μνήσῃ ’whenever anyone mentions’) · also + opt., of what may happen in time to come: ’whenever he should’ (ὁππότε νοστήσειε ’whenever he should come home’) · also + indic., of a recurring case: ’whenever’ (ὁππότε θυμὸς ἄνωγε ’whenever the heart bids’) · also + fut. indic., after a verb of waiting: ‘for the moment when’ (δέγμενος … ὁππότε … ἐφήσει ‘waiting for when he will lay on’) · also + indic., of a single past occasion: ’when’ (ὁππότε … ἐέλπετο ’when she supposed’) · also + opt., of what recurs: ’whenever’ (ὁππότε … ἐπιβρίσειαν ’whenever … press down’)
ὁρόων: ὁράω — see; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic stretched (= Attic ὁρῶν): ’seeing’
ὄλυμπον: Ὄλυμπος — Olympus, home of the gods; masc. acc. sg.
ὅππως: ὅπως — how, in what way; epic ὅππως (double π metri gratia), with κε + subj. (or fut.): ’how you are to…’ · also + opt. in an indirect question after a past verb: ’how he might’ (ὅππως νοστήσει’ … ’how he might return’)
ὅτ: ὅτε (elided ὅτ’) — when; temporal conj., here + ἄν and subj. in a general/future clause · also + indic., of a single definite past event: ’when’ (ὅτ’ ἐν Ἄργεϊ ... ἵστασαν ’when they were mooring in Argos’) · also + opt., in a repeated past clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτ’ ἂψ ἄρχοιτο ’whenever he began again’) · also + subj. without ἄν, in a general clause: ὅτ’ … ἔχῃ ’whenever … holds’ · also in ὡς ὅτ’, ’as when (a minstrel does)’, the verb left unexpressed · also in ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ introducing a simile with a finite verb expressed: ’as when’ (ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ … ἁλιεὺς … προΐησι) · also causal + indic.: ’since, because’ (ὅτ’ οὐκ ἐθέλουσι δικαίως ’since they are not willing to act justly’) · also + opt., of a time conceived as possible: ’when’ (ὅτ’ … λιποίμην ’when I should be left behind’) · also in ὡς ὅτ’ introducing a simile with the finite verb expressed: ’as when’ (ὡς ὅτ’ ἀνὴρ … ἐτάνυσσε ’as when a man … stretches’)
ὑγρὰ: ὑγρός — wet, fluid, liquid; neut. acc. pl.
ὑψιβρεμέτης: ὑψιβρεμέτης — high-thundering (ὑψι- ’on high’ + βρέμω ’thunder, roar’); standing epithet of Zeus, masc. nom. sg.
ᾗσιν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσιν: ’in his own (mind)’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: which; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσιν: ’in which’ (ᾗσιν ἀγαλλόμενοι ’taking pride in which’)
ᾠχόμεθ: οἴχομαι — go, be gone; impf. 1 pl., augmented ᾠ-, elided (ᾠχόμεθ’ = ᾠχόμεθα): ’we went’
ῥίγιον: ῥίγιον — colder, harsher, worse (cf. ῥῖγος ’cold’); comparative adj., neut. nom. sg., predicate: ’colder’
